newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian rebels seized Permet in south before deal.
newsitem.headline: Albanian rebels seized Permet in south before deal.

text.p: Albanian rebels seized another important southern town, Permet, before President Sali Berisha struck a deal on Sunday to hold elections, rebels and residents coming from the area said on Monday.
The rebels and residents said six people were killed in the fighting in Permet on Sunday. They were arriving in rebel-held Gjirokaster, a main southern town and military base.
There was no independent confirmation. Permet is on the main highway going southeast from rebel-held Tepelene. A base near Permet was used for staging a failed army raid on Gjirokaster last week.
The travellers gave no further details on the fighting. Rebel leaders in Gjirokaster also said Permet had fallen and government troops had fled.
Berisha, facing a growing armed revolt in the south, agreed with all political parties to hold a new general election in June -- three years ahead of schedule.

Rebels in the south greeted the news coolly, saying they wanted Berisha himself to resign before surrendering thousands of weapons -- including tanks and heavy artillery -- which have been looted from state arsenals.
Berisha is accused by the rebels of standing by while five fraudulent pyramid investment schemes collapsed in January, wiping out the savings of thousands of Albanians.
The armed revolt began in the Adriatic coastal town of Vlore and spread throughout the southwest corner of the country.

Rebel leaders, many former army officers, were in contact on Monday in the main towns of Gjirokaster, Vlore, Sarande and Delvine to discuss Berisha's deal with opposition parties. They said they would discuss the agreement with opposition leaders in Tirana as well.
